title: Acceptance bound from a large Fourier coefficient
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\phi:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb R$ be pointwise nonnegative with uniform mean $1$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$. Suppose $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $|\widehat\phi(\gamma)|\leq\varepsilon$ for every nonzero $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$, where $\widehat\phi$ denotes the Fourier coefficient with respect to the uniform measure. If some $\gamma_0\in\mathbb F_2^n$ satisfies $\tfrac12\leq\widehat F(\gamma_0)^2$, where $F(x)=(-1)^{f(x)}$, then
\[2\Pr_{x,\ y\sim\phi}[f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)]-1\leq\varepsilon+(1-\varepsilon)\widehat F(\gamma_0)^2,\]
with $x$ uniform and $y$ drawn according to $\phi$ relative to uniform measure.
hypotheses_covered: A vector $\gamma_0$ whose squared Fourier coefficient of $F$ is at least $1/2$
